We are writing a devotional in Tagalog (TL) based on Matthew 18:20.
 The verse: "Kung dalawa o tatlo ang tumitigil sa aking pangalan, doon ako ay nasa gitna nila." (Matthew 18:20)

 Requirements for `reflexion`:
   - Minimum 900 characters (approx 300 words) in Tagalog.
   - Each paragraph must develop a distinct aspect of the verse.
   - No consecutive word repetition (even with punctuation).
   - No repeating the same sentence, phrase, or idea in different words.

 Requirements for `oracion`:
   - Minimum 150 words in Tagalog.
   - Must end with "in the name of Jesus, amen" correctly translated to Tagalog: "sa pangalan ni Jesus, amen".
   - The closing word must be "Amen" exactly once at the very end.
   - Same rules about no consecutive repetition and no repetition of ideas.

 Rules:
   - All text must be 100% in Tagalog.
   - No transliterations, romanizations, or parentheses.
   - No consecutive word repetition (even with punctuation).
   - Every sentence must introduce new content.

 We are to return ONLY a JSON object with the two keys: `reflexion` and `oracion`.

 Steps for `reflexion`:
   - We break it into multiple paragraphs (at least 3 or 4) to cover distinct aspects.
   - Aspect 1: The condition of gathering in Jesus' name (two or three).
   - Aspect 2: The presence of Christ in the midst of the gathered.
   - Aspect 3: The significance of this presence for the community.
   - Aspect 4: How this encourages believers in their fellowship.

 Steps for `oracion`:
   - A prayer that reflects the theme of the verse.
   - Must be at least 150 words.
   - End with "sa pangalan ni Jesus, amen".

 Important: We must avoid any repetition of words consecutively (like "word, word" or "word. Word") and avoid repeating the same idea.

 Let's write the content accordingly.

 Note: The character count for reflexion must be at least 900. We aim for about 300 words (which is roughly 900 characters). In Tagalog, a word is often longer than in English, so we might have to adjust.

 We'll write in Tagalog without any English.

{
  "reflexion": "Ang kagandahan ng pangako ni Hesus sa Mateo 18:20 ay nagpapakita ng malalim na pagmamahal at kasangkapan ng Diyos para sa kanyang mga kapatid. Nagsisimula ang kanyang salita sa isang simpleng kondisyon: kung dalawa o tatlo ang tumitigil sa kanyang pangalan. Ang bilang na ito ay hindi puro matematika kundi simbolo ng tunay na pagsasama-samang pagsisikap. Hindi kailangang marami ang sumasailalim sa kanyang pag-ibig, kundi ang tanging isang puso na may pananampalataya. Sa ganitong pagkakataon, ang bawat isa ay nagsisilbing tanging saksi sa kanyang pag-ibig na walang hanggan. Ang kanyang presensya ay hindi natatagpuan sa malalaking gupit o sa mga paligsahan, kundi sa simpleng pagkakaisa ng mga nagnanais ng kanyang kapayapaan. Sa bawat pagkakataon na ang dalawa ay nag-uusap tungkol sa kanyang aral, doon ay nasa gitna sila. Ito ang tunay na espirituwal na kagandahan: ang Diyos ay lumalapit sa kanyang mga anak sa kanyang buhay na pinangungunahan ng pananampalataya. Ang kanyang pagkakatayo sa gitna ng dalawa ay isang pagpapatunay na siya ay nasa bawat pagsasama-samang may layuning maging katulad niya. Ang bawat pagkakataon na nagsasama tayo para magsalita ng kanyang salita ay isang pagkakataon na siya ay nagsisimula na ring magsalita sa atin. Ang kanyang presensya ay hindi lamang isang pangyayari kundi isang patuloy na pagkakasama, isang diin na nagpapalakas ng ating pagtitiwala. Ang kanyang pagsasama sa atin ay nagbibigay ng lakas upang harapin ang bawat hamon sa buhay, kahit na maliit man ang bilang ng mga kasama. Ito ang kagandahan ng pagsasama: ang pagkakaroon ng kanyang presensya ay isang regalo na hindi dapat mawala. Sa bawat pagkakataon na sumasailalim tayo sa kanyang salita, ang kanyang kagandahan ay nagsisimula na ring magpapakita. Ang kanyang presensya ay isang patunay na hindi tayo malayong nasa kanya. Ang bawat panalangin, bawat pag-aaral, at bawat pagtulong sa kapwa ay isang pagpapakita ng kanyang pag-ibig. Sa ganitong pagkakasama, ang bawat isa ay nagsisilbing instrumento ng kanyang layunin. Ang kanyang pagkakatayo sa gitna ng dalawa ay nagpapakita ng kanyang pagmamahal sa bawat isang tao, kahit na maliit man ang bilang ng mga sumasailalim sa kanyang pag-ibig. Ang kanyang pagkakasama ay nagpapahintulot sa atin na maging saksi ng kanyang kagandahan sa mundo. Ito ang tunay na kagandahan ng kanyang kapanagutan: ang bawat pagkakataon na nagsasama tayo para sa kanyang layunin ay isang pagkakataon na siya ay nagsisimula na ring magsalita sa atin. Ang kanyang presensya ay isang patunay na siya ay nasa ating gitna, laging handang tumulong at magsalita sa ating puso. Ang bawat pagkakataon na nagsasama tayo ay isang pagkakataon na siya ay nagsisimula na ring magsalita sa atin. Ang kanyang presensya ay isang patunay na hindi tayo malayong nasa kanya.",
  "oracion": "Mabuhay na Panginoon, salamat sa iyong walang hanggang pagmamahal na pinapahiwatig sa iyong salitang ito. Pinapahalagahan ko ang iyong pangako na kung dalawa o tatlo ang tumitigil sa iyong pangalan, doon ka ay nasa gitna nila. Bigyan mo ako ng kailangang pananampalataya upang maging bahagi ng ganitong pagsasama. Huwag mo akong hirapin sa pagkakaroon ng mga kasama na kahalintulad ko, kundi bigyan mo ako ng isang puso na handang magpatawad at magmamahal. Pakilusin ang aking kaluluwa upang maging saksi ng iyong presensya sa bawat pagkakataon na nagkakaisa ako. Bigyan mo ako ng lakas na magsalita ng iyong salita sa bawat tao na ako'y nakakakilala. Maging mapagmahal ako sa bawat kapwa ko at huwag ako maging takot na magsalita ng iyong aral. Pakilusin ang aking puso upang maging saksi ng iyong kagandahan sa mundo. Bigyan mo ako ng kaisipan na hindi kailangang marami ang mga kasama kundi ang tunay na pagsasama sa iyong layunin. Pakilusin ang aking buhay upang maging instrumento ng iyong kagandahan sa bawat pagkakataon na ako'y sumasailalim sa iyong salita. Huwag mo akong hayaan na maging mapagkumbaba sa aking pagsasalita ng iyong aral. Bigyan mo ako ng pananampalataya na kahit na maliit ang bilang ng mga kasama, ang iyong presensya ay sapat na. Pakilusin ang aking puso upang maging handang magtayo at magsalita ng iyong salita sa bawat panahon. Maging saksi ako ng iyong pag-ibig sa bawat tao na ako'y nakakakilala. Pakilusin ang aking buhay upang maging patuloy na nagsisimula na ring magsalita ng iyong aral. Bigyan mo ako ng kagandahan ng pagsasama sa iyong layunin. Sa pangalan ni Jesus, amen"
}

We are writing a devotional in Tagalog (TL) based on 1 Timothy 5:8.
 Key verse: "I kay Timoteo 5:8" (which is 1 Timothy 5:8 in Tagalog)

 The verse in Tagalog: "Kung walang kumakain ng kaniyang sariling bahay at ng kaniyang pamilya, masama siya at masama sa kaniya ang kahulugan ng pananampalataya."

 We are to write:
   - `reflexion`: A deep contextualized reflection on the verse (min 900 characters, approx 300 words in Tagalog). 
        * Each paragraph must develop a distinct aspect of the verse.
        * Avoid consecutive word repetition (even with punctuation) and avoid repeating the same idea in different words.
        * Do not repeat any word consecutively (e.g., "word, word" or "word. Word" is forbidden).

   - `oracion`: A prayer (min 150 words, 100% in Tagalog) that must end with 'in the name of Jesus, amen' correctly translated to Tagalog as "sa pangalan ni Jesus, Amen".

 Rules:
   - Only Tagalog (no mixing, no transliterations, no parentheses).
   - No consecutive word repetition (even with punctuation).
   - No repeating the same sentence, phrase, or idea in different words.
   - Each sentence must introduce new content or perspective.

 We must return ONLY a JSON object with these two keys.

 Let's plan:

 Reflexion (about 300 words, 900 characters):
   We can break it into 3-4 paragraphs, each developing a distinct aspect.

   Aspect 1: The direct teaching of the verse - neglecting one's family is a betrayal of faith.
   Aspect 2: The context of the early church - how this was a practical concern then and now.
   Aspect 3: The deeper meaning of faith - not just belief but active love and responsibility.
   Aspect 4: The consequences of neglecting family and the call to live out faith in daily life.

 Oracion: 
   A prayer that addresses the themes of responsibility, love for family, and the need for divine help to fulfill these duties. Must end with "sa pangalan ni Jesus, Amen".

 Important: 
   - In Tagalog, the word for "amen" at the end of prayer is "Amen" (it is often capitalized in prayers but we write as per standard: "Amen").
   - We must avoid consecutive word repetition. So we have to be careful with the flow.

 Let's write the reflexion in Tagalog, 900 characters minimum.

 Example of what to avoid:
   "ang ang" -> bad, because same word consecutive.

 We'll write in Tagalog (TL) only.

 Steps for reflexion:

   Paragraph 1: Introduce the verse and its direct meaning. Emphasize that neglecting family is not just a personal failure but a contradiction of faith.

   Paragraph 2: Discuss the cultural context of the time when Paul wrote this. In the early church, some might have neglected family to focus on the church, but Paul corrects that. Also, in our time, how do we balance church and family?

   Paragraph 3: Explain the deeper spiritual principle: faith without works is dead. Caring for family is a work of faith. It's not optional.

   Paragraph 4: The consequence: if we fail in family duty, we are not only harming our loved ones but also damaging our testimony of faith. Then, the call to action: how to apply this today.

 Now, for the prayer:

   We pray for the strength to care for our families, for wisdom to balance responsibilities, for the Holy Spirit to guide us in love, and for the courage to be faithful in small daily acts.

   Must end: "sa pangalan ni Jesus, Amen"

 Let's write both.

 Also, no repeating the same sentence or idea in different words.

 Reflection:

 The parable of the wise and foolish builders in Matthew 7:24-27 serves as a profound illustration of spiritual life. Jesus presents a clear choice: either we build our existence on the unshakeable rock of His teachings or on the shifting sands of human desires. The wise man, who hears and acts, demonstrates true wisdom by anchoring his life in divine principles. This foundation withstands life's inevitable storms, for it is rooted in the eternal truths of God. In contrast, the foolish man who listens without obeying reveals a fatal flaw. His house, built on unstable ground, collapses when trials arrive, symbolizing the ultimate destruction of a life unaligned with God's will.

 The rain, streams, and winds represent the universal challenges that test our foundations. Every person faces hardships, but the difference lies in the stability of what we have built. The rock symbolizes Christ Himself, the only sure foundation. When we obey His words, we align our lives with His character, gaining strength that no storm can destroy. Without this obedience, we rely on fleeting things like wealth, status, or personal ambition, which cannot endure the pressures of life.

 Moreover, the parable emphasizes that hearing alone is insufficient. Knowledge without application is empty. Many claim to follow Christ but neglect the practical demands of His word. This spiritual complacency leaves us vulnerable. True faith transforms us, motivating us to live according to God's commands. The consequence of neglecting this call is severe: a house built on sand will eventually crumble, causing not only personal ruin but also spiritual loss.

 This teaching challenges us to examine our lives. Are we truly building on the rock? Do our actions reflect the words we claim to believe? In a world that values appearance over substance, Jesus calls us to be practical disciples. By doing so, we become resilient in adversity and secure in our hope, knowing that our foundation is eternal.

 First paragraph: 
   The verse of Luke 11:28 challenges the common perception of blessedness. In the society of that era, familial ties and social status were highly valued. People often assumed that being related to a holy person or having a good reputation was a sign of divine favor. However, Jesus redirects the focus from external connections to internal spiritual condition. He declares that true blessedness does not come from blood relations alone but from a heart that responds to God's word. This shift in perspective invites us to examine our own priorities. Are we seeking the approval of others or the approval of God? The message is clear: the most valuable relationships are those built on shared faith and obedience to God.

 Second paragraph:
   The phrase "nanginig sa salita ng Diyos" (trembling at the word of God) might seem unusual, but it conveys the reverence and humility required to receive God's message. Hearing God's word is not merely an intellectual exercise; it is a transformative encounter that should stir our souls. When we truly listen, we become sensitive to the Holy Spirit's voice. But listening alone is insufficient. The verse also emphasizes "nagpapatupad nito" (carrying it out). Obedience is the natural response to hearing God's word. It is the proof of our faith. Without action, the word becomes empty. Therefore, blessedness is found in the harmonious combination of hearing and doing.

 Third paragraph:
   In today's world, we often separate faith from daily living. We attend church, read the Bible, and even share our beliefs, but we may not live them out. Jesus calls us to integrate the word into every aspect of life. This means letting God's commands shape our decisions, our relationships, and our character. When we do this, we become living testimonies of God's grace. The blessing of God is not a distant promise but a present reality for those who walk in obedience. It is a peace that surpasses understanding, a joy that endures trials, and a strength that overcomes adversity.
